label: Blue Note (BLP 4104 / BST 84104)
rationale: Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers' Blue Note sextet session with Freddie Hubbard, Curtis Fuller, Wayne Shorter, Cedar Walton and Jymie Merritt — recorded November 28 and December 18, 1961 at Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs, released July 1963 as BLP 4104/BST 84104. The same frontline (Hubbard, Shorter) that fed Miles Davis' 1960s quintet is documented here at Blue Note peak: three Shorter compositions (Backstage Sally, Contemplation, Reincarnation Blues), Fuller's title cut Bu's Delight, Walton's Shaky Jake, and the Mancini-Mercer ballad Moon River. Ratings as reported by Wikipedia: AllMusic 4 stars, Down Beat 4.5, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 4, Penguin Guide 4. This is the missing high-gravity sextet Blakey date in a canon that already carries Moanin', Mosaic, Ugetsu and Free for All — session gravity (the Hubbard/Shorter/Fuller frontline) and defining-statement signals both clear.

personnel_record.notes: Two sessions, same sextet. November 28, 1961: Contemplation and Moon River (issued) plus four alternate takes (Backstage Sally alt, Bu's Delight alt, Reincarnation Blues alt, Moon River alt) that became CD bonus tracks. December 18, 1961: Backstage Sally, Bu's Delight, Reincarnation Blues, Shaky Jake. All ten tracks carry the full sextet; no per-track personnel variation is documented, so track_assignments_complete is false. Album released July 1963 (Blue Note BLP 4104 mono / BST 84104 stereo) after Blakey moved to Riverside; the 1992 CD (CDP 7 84104 2) added the four alternates. AllMusic catalogues the recording year as 1962 and mentions 'New York, NY' alongside Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs in its location blurb; session-level sources (jazzdisco #611128/#611218, Discogs) document Englewood Cliffs only.

ballot.album: Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers — Buhaina's Delight (1963)
ballot.case_for: Session gravity is the signal here — the Hubbard/Shorter/Fuller/Walton/Merritt sextet is a load-bearing personnel network captured at Van Gelder in late 1961, and Shorter's three originals (notably 'Contemplation,' a widely covered standard) document his compositional voice forming audibly two to three years before JuJu and his move to Miles' second quintet. Four independent ratings — AllMusic 4★, Down Beat 4½, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 4, Penguin Guide 4 — confirm real consensus across traditions of listing. The record sits in the same Blue Note run as the already-canonized Mosaic and Free for All but adds the trombone-voiced sextet color and a lyrical Moon River ballad reading that a cold listener would immediately understand as hard-bop.
ballot.case_against: The defining-statement signal is moderate at best — Moanin' owns that slot for Blakey, and Free for All and Ugetsu each have stronger individual claims. This exact sextet debuted weeks earlier on Mosaic (1961) and hit its apex on Free for All (1964); Buhaina's Delight is essentially the second chapter of that same unbroken run, raising the honest question of whether it teaches a listener something those two do not already cover. The consensus evidence is reported as star ratings rather than critical essays — the Penguin crown status is unresolved — and all five dossier sources are metadata or identifier pages, none a retrospective analysis.
ballot.disagreement: The references split on tier: one argues 'contested' (catalog depth and thin sourcing are genuine counterweights), the other 'consensus_core' (the against-case is too thin to derail it). Both agree on 'strong' priority.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John weigh this as a strong contested date — the session-gravity and Shorter-lineage arguments are genuine and rubric-aligned, but he should decide whether a fifth Blakey title earns its place when Mosaic and Free for All already document this exact sextet.
